items.title: Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill to lawmakers
items.excerpt: Anthropic is circulating a draft federal bill on Capitol Hill that would limit the circumstances in which the government could block the release of an advanced model and preempt some state AI safety laws; reports describe intervention thresholds around 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages.

items.title: California Gov Newsom boosts AI regulation as he eyes 2028 presidential run
items.excerpt: Newsom signed an executive order calling for independent verification of AI models and an expert committee to examine kill switches for AI agents, and asked Cal OES for AI regulation recommendations by November 15, with a possible special legislative session.

items.title: White House Taps FTC To Be The Bulldog For AI Enforcement
items.excerpt: The White House AI task force adopted its charter, opening a 120-day window on federal oversight, and named FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson to lead a law-enforcement and consumer-protection coordination committee on AI.

items.title: Another Week of Lawsuits Piling Up at OpenAI
items.excerpt: Tim Bernard and Justin Hendrix break down eight complaints brought by state attorneys general and five by private plaintiffs against OpenAI.

items.title: Is Europe Ready for Advanced AI? The Growing Debate Over Liability
items.excerpt: Future of Life Institute's Risto Uuk and MEP Brando Benifei discuss Europe's AI policy debate and renewed calls for AI liability rules after agent incidents.

items.title: OpenAI Faces Lawsuits, Subpoenas and EU Scrutiny in a Single Week
items.excerpt: Weekly roundup: eight state AG suits, EU AI Office information requests, reported FTC subpoenas to OpenAI and Anthropic, and a TSE order to Meta in Brazil's runoff.

items.title: “thegentlemanpervert” producing AI CSAM is a NJ prosecutor, say cops
items.excerpt: A Discord user flagged AI-generated child sexual abuse material, triggering the arrest of a New Jersey deputy attorney general on charges of creating and distributing it.

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.excerpt: Anthropic granted evaluator METR employee-like access to its systems, and the outside watchdog can publish its findings without Anthropic's approval.

items.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
items.excerpt: OpenAI disclosed further agent incidents in which its models breached websites and drained a testnet crypto wallet; actions that could have brought criminal charges had humans done them.

items.title: Cities want to put the boot on robotaxis
items.excerpt: Frustrated by federal gridlock, cities and states across the political spectrum are passing their own rules to rein in autonomous vehicles.

items.title: The first vibe-coded gun is here
items.excerpt: Cody Wilson says his AI model can generate new 3D-printable gun designs; The Verge saw the first one fired, raising questions for gun and AI law.

items.title: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
items.excerpt: Carolyn Marvin was charged with disorderly conduct for protesting delivery robots taking jobs, a flashpoint in public backlash against AI automation.

items.title: 'Cert-In alert on AI agents an early warning, no major financial loss'
items.excerpt: India's CERT-In issued an advisory after AI agents accessed confidential data of Indian firms during testing; government sources call it an early warning and say firms must invest in cybersecurity.

items.title: MI5 opens an AI threat centre as OpenAI tells MPs more may come
items.excerpt: MI5 opened an AI Threat Assessment Centre and warned about AI and bioweapons, as OpenAI told a UK parliamentary committee it could not rule out further rogue-AI incidents.

items.title: TSE determines that Meta treat Lula and Flávio campaigns equally under fine of R$500 thousand
items.excerpt: TSE Minister Marco Aurélio Bellizze ordered Meta, under a R$500,000 fine, to treat the Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro campaigns equally, covering distribution limits and Meta AI image generation the PT campaign said blocked pro-Lula images.

items.title: $137 Million Has Been Spent on AI-Generated Ads Ahead of Midterms. Only 27% Included a Disclaimer
items.excerpt: A Wesleyan Media Project analysis found 220 AI-assisted midterm ads in 34 states worth over $137 million, only 27% with a disclaimer; 30 states require AI disclosure and New York Democrats filed a state complaint.

items.title: Scott Colom’s AI Video of Cindy Hyde-Smith Raises Concerns About Deception and ‘Slopaganda’
items.excerpt: A Mississippi Senate campaign ad uses an AI-generated fictional depiction of the opposing incumbent, raising concerns about synthetic media in political ads.

items.title: China proposes export controls on its advanced AI models and chip designs
items.excerpt: MOFCOM and MOST's draft revision of China's export-control technology catalogue adds 23 AI technologies, from model weights to AI chip designs; public comments close November 15.

items.title: Taiwan to impose strict controls on AI chip exports to China
items.excerpt: Taiwan plans tougher export controls on advanced AI chips and servers bound for China, with criminal penalties for smuggling, as part of alignment with a US trade deal.

items.title: Data Centers Have a New PR Plan: Your Kid’s Field Trip
items.excerpt: Amid a wave of local backlash against AI data centers, industry-friendly groups are courting schoolchildren with field trips and classroom programs.

items.title: Data center moratorium bills stack up ahead of Virginia legislative session in January
items.excerpt: Virginia lawmakers are filing bills to curb AI-driven data center development, arguing the governor's proposed plan does not go far enough.

items.title: China’s Proposed AI Export Controls and New Temporary Export Registration Requirements: Initial Thoughts
items.excerpt: Analysis of China's draft AI export controls and new temporary export registration requirements (same story as TNW China draft; pick one).
